text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Danish securities dealers are strongly opposed to adopting a proposed Swedish rule banning closed-door company meetings with analysts.

--- A new European Commission survey on crime in European cities now shows that Denmark is the place in the EU where people fell most safe with only 11 percent of the Danes questioned feeling unsafe in the streets at night compared to 60 percent in former East Germany.

--- Swedish telecom company Telia now claims that several competitors, among which is Danish telecom group Tele Danmark, are not paying enough for using Telia telephone lines, depriving Telia of several hundred million crowns a year. A number of court cases between Telia and other telecom companies for breaking competition rules are now on their way.
--- Danes aim to save money on telephone bills has now led to a regular rush on new operators on the Danish telecom market.
--- Large Danish pension funds are increasingly placing money abroad meaning that Danish pensions are increasingly dependent on the performance of groups like VW, British Airways, Saab and Bayer.
--- Denmark is close to the top in the European Union when it comes to economic growth with a GDP increase of 1.02 percent in the first quarter of 1996, a new European Commission report shows.
